correctness.rationale: Riemann–Hurwitz for a tame cyclic cubic covering branched at four simple quartic roots and infinity gives genus three. On regular differentials dx/y², xdx/y², dx/y, Cartier coefficient extraction and evenness of x-quartic produce 3x3 sparse blocks. The relevant coefficients E,G,A factor, mod p, as nonzero multiples of (T²-1)^r H, (T²-1)^r, and (T²-1)^(r+1) H respectively. Lucas binomial vanishing provides endpoint powers; Gegenbauer ODE and its unique polynomial solution of degree ≤r prove proportionality; highest T coefficients give degree exactly r and values at ±1 are nonzero. value.rationale: The family is a canonical genus-three bielliptic Picard pencil, and the distribution of p-rank, a-number and Newton strata is a natural arithmetic invariant. An explicit squarefree parameter-level Hasse divisor uniform in p provides exact loci for a geometrically meaningful superspecial/nonordinary transition, useful beyond a small prime table; it is structurally derived from Cartier and Shimura/Prym decomposition.
residual_risks: All-prime proof is not finite enumeration; full specialized Shimura comparison remains a historical risk.

final_claim: For all primes p>=5 and the smooth marked family y^3=x^4+2tx^2+1 over algebraic closure with t!=±1, the explicit coefficient H_p(T)=[u^{3r}](u^2+2Tu+1)^{2r} when p=6r+1 and [u^{3r+2}](u^2+2Tu+1)^{2r+1} when p=6r+5, r=floor((p-1)/6), has precisely r simple geometric roots outside ±1; it gives complete four-row p-rank, a-number and Newton polygon stratification including superspecial points when p≡5 mod6 and H_p(t)=0.
